speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the Ministry has studied the effectiveness of the enforcement powers provided to inspectors with the Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals in England and Wales and officers with the American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider providing similar enforcement powers under the Animals and Birds Act to selected non-Government animal welfare groups in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Beyond putting in place laws and regulations, we take a multi-stakeholder approach to prevent cruelty to animals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, we work closely with stakeholders such as animal welfare groups and veterinarians to raise public awareness on responsible pet ownership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We also take a serious view of all acts of animal cruelty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks investigates all feedback on animal abuse and will not hesitate to take the appropriate enforcement action.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I do understand that we have an increasing number of animal welfare cases and complaints, as well, and also very limited manpower at AVS.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, could I ask whether we could study, not extending enforcement powers to all animal welfare groups, but maybe a select few, like the SPCA, who is already investigating animal cruelty on the ground?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Two, I thank the Senior Minister of State for saying that they are going to review international practices, but could we also review local ones where we have NEA already having the community volunteer programme, where they have basic enforcement powers given out to members of the public.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, whether MND can review that programme and see whether it can extend it also to AVA's work?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I sympathise and empathise with where the Member is coming from.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Our NParks officers and our relevant officers who are delegated the powers to investigate, look into every single feedback seriously.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In fact, most of the time, they are feedback around nuisance about animals, for example, poor hygiene, smell or sometime, just neighbourly disputes.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: That is where we work very closely with the animal welfare groups.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They are valuable partners and stakeholders in this effort, raising public awareness, looking into those issues and making sure that cases are followed up quickly and expeditiously.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, I thank the Member for his suggestions and feedback.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is something we will continue to look at.

speaker: Mr Speaker
